title: Onboarding Concierge — First 30 Days Activation Manual
author: Sofia Chen
body:
Overview:

This document defines the Onboarding Concierge program and the operational playbook for activating new contributors during their first 30 days at Redwood. The Concierge program is a lightweight, coordinated service run by People Ops that centralizes access provisioning, role activation, and early-stage success checkpoints so new hires can reach contribution velocity faster.

Scope and goals:

- Scope: all full-time hires, contractors with >= 30 days assignment, and long-term interns. Does not cover short-term consultants (<30 days) unless flagged by hiring manager.
- Primary goals:
  - Reach baseline productivity: first PR/feature/assignment submitted by day 14 for ICs, or first project milestone for managers.
  - Remove tooling friction: 95% of required accounts and permissions provisioned by day 3.
  - Early alignment: onboarding plan reviewed with manager and concierge within 48 hours of start.

Concierge responsibilities (People Ops):

1. Pre-boarding (T-5 to T-1):
   - Coordinate with hiring manager to confirm role profile, team repo lists, and required systems.
   - Trigger automated provisioning in Redwood Access Portal (RAP): Okta group assignments, GCP project request, Slack channel invites, JIRA board access.
   - Prepare role activation packet and Slack DM template for manager + buddy.

2. Day 0 and Day 1:
   - Day 0: ensure equipment delivery and basic network/VPN instructions are sent. Verify device enrollment in MDM.
   - Day 1: run 30-minute concierge welcome call covering critical first-week tasks, who to contact for emergencies, and how to access the First-30 checklist.

3. Days 2–7:
   - Verify access to source control, CI/CD pipelines, artifact registries, and internal docs. Conduct access remediation if any step fails.
   - Assign a temporary contributor tag in the onboarding tracking sheet (People Ops owned).

4. Days 8–30:
   - Facilitate check-ins (Day 14 and Day 28) to confirm role ramp, unblock infrastructure or permission issues, and record manager feedback.

First-30 timeline (high level):

Day -5 to -1 (Pre-boarding):
- Hiring manager completes Role Activation Request (RAR) form: team, repos, infra projects, training modules.
- Concierge verifies RAR and starts RAP provisioning.

Day 0 (Start):
1. New hire receives welcome kit + equipment tracking link.
2. Concierge sends Day 1 schedule and 1:1 to manager.

Day 1 (Orientation):
- 30-min concierge call.
- Account checklist walkthrough.
- Assign buddy and first task.

Day 2–3 (Access verification):
- Confirm GitHub access, internal container registry, CI runner tokens, internal wiki, and Slack channels.
- If any access fails, escalate to Identity Operations (IdOps) within 4 business hours.

Day 4–7 (Environment setup):
- Ensure local dev environment compiles with standard build command and tests run locally.
- Concierge logs setup status and open issues.

Day 8–14 (First contributions):
- New hire completes onboarding issue: small bug fix or doc improvement.
- Manager and buddy review first PR within 3 business days.

Day 15–30 (Stabilization):
- Remove temporary elevated permissions and confirm least-privilege posture.
- Final 30-day review meeting scheduled and recorded in HRIS.

Role activation checklist (table):

| Item | Owner | Target day | Success criteria |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| Accept offer & sign agreements | People Ops | -5 | Signed in HRIS |
| Device + MDM enrollment | IT Ops | 0 | Device shows as enrolled in MDM console |
| Okta account and SSO access | IdOps | 0 | Login success and 2FA configured |
| Slack & email | People Ops | 0 | In org Slack and mailbox receives test message |
| GitHub access + team membership | Team admin/Manager | 1 | Can clone internal repos and create branches |
| CI runner token & Docker registry | Infra | 2 | Can run pipeline and pull/push test artifacts |
| Project-specific infra access (GCP/AWS) | Infra | 3 | IAM role assigned and can view project resources |
| JIRA board and issue assignment | Manager | 3 | Can view and transition issues |
| Internal training modules assigned | People Ops | 3 | Modules in LMS assigned and first module completed |
| Security awareness training completed | Security | 7 | Completion recorded in LMS and badge granted |

Access matrix (common roles):

- Engineering IC (Backend): GitHub: write to team repos, GCP: viewer + deployer role for staging projects, JIRA: edit.
- Infra/Platform: GitHub: admin for infra repos, GCP: editor for infra projects, Jenkins/CI tokens.
- Product/PM: GitHub: read for public and internal docs, JIRA: admin for product boards, Amplitude: analyst.

Automations, scripts and runbooks:

- RAP (Redwood Access Portal) flows used by Concierge: rdp-trigger-provision.sh (invokes RAP API), rap-status-checker.py (status polling).
- Example CLI: 
  - rap provision: curl -X POST https://rap.redwood.internal/api/v1/provision -H 'Authorization: Bearer $RAP_TOKEN' -d '{"email":"new.hire@redwood.com","role":"engineer","components":["github","gcp:staging"]}'
- People Ops automation repo: git@github.com:redwood/people-ops/onboarding-automations.git (contains templates and Terraform wrappers).

Troubleshooting and escalation path:

1. Missing Okta/SSO access -> file IdOps ticket via internal JIRA project ONB-OPS with priority P1 if >4 business hours impact.
2. CI token not working -> Infra pager; escalation matrix below:
   - Weekdays 09:00–18:00: Infra oncall -> infra-team@redwood.com -> PagerDuty.
   - Off-hours: SRE oncall -> PagerDuty emergency channel.
3. Device not enrolling -> IT Ops ticket and temporary remote dev container provided: devbox.redwood.internal.

Ownership and SLAs:

- People Ops (Concierge) owns 0–7 day SLA: 95% of checklists must be green by Day 3.
- IdOps owns 0–2 day SLA for Okta provisioning.
- Infra owns 0–3 day SLA for cloud IAM roles and CI tokens.
- Manager owns First-PR review SLA: review completed within 3 business days.

Onboarding success metrics (tracked monthly):

- Time-to-first-PR (median) — target <= 14 days.
- Access completion rate by Day 3 — target >= 95%.
- New-hire NPS after 30 days — target >= 8.0.
- Percentage requiring manual escalations after Day 7 — target <= 10%.

Manager & peer responsibilities:

- Manager must submit a Role Activation Request (RAR) no later than 7 calendar days before start. RAR template link: [RAR form internal link].
- Manager assigns a buddy for the first 30 days and blocks 2 hours in Week 1 for paired work.
- Buddy performs first-PR walkthrough and documents review checklist in the onboarding tracker.

Templates and links (internal):

- RAR form: https://redwood.atlassian.net/secure/RAR-form (internal)
- Onboarding tracker (People Ops sheet): https://sheets.internal.redwood.com/onboarding-tracker
- RAP API docs: https://rap.redwood.internal/docs
- People Ops automation repo: git@github.com:redwood/people-ops/onboarding-automations.git

Security & least-privilege considerations:

- Temporary elevated access given for environment setup must be timeboxed and removed automatically by onboarding automations at Day 14 unless manager re-authorizes.
- Sensitive infra roles (production deployer, DB admin) require explicit manager approval and an approval ticket in JIRA with Security reviewer sign-off.

Audit, reporting and record-keeping:

- All provisioning actions are logged in RAP and forwarded to the Security audit log service (audit.redwood.internal) with the following fields: actor, target_user, components_changed, timestamp, request_id.
- People Ops will export a monthly onboarding report that includes the success metrics above and a list of manual escalations.
